Claude responded: Let's fix this.

Let's fix this. A few quick questions to figure out exactly what's happening:

Waiting for your answers — those two things will tell me exactly what the issue is and how to fix it.

In the meantime, here's what most commonly goes wrong with GoDaddy nameservers:

The #1 issue — GoDaddy has two different DNS screens and people often edit the wrong one. There's a "DNS Records" page (where you manage A records, CNAMEs etc.) and a separate "Nameservers" section at the very bottom of that same page. The nameservers section is easy to miss. You need the Nameservers section specifically — not the DNS records table at the top.

The #2 issue — timing. DNS propagation can take anywhere from 10 minutes to 48 hours depending on your internet provider. If it's been under a few hours, it may just need more time.

The #3 issue — Netlify domain setup wasn't completed fully on their side. Even after you change GoDaddy's nameservers, Netlify needs to have the domain added to your site in their dashboard, otherwise it won't route correctly.

Once you answer above I can walk you through the exact fix step by step.

Claude responded: That's completely normal — you're in the waiting zone!

That's completely normal — you're in the waiting zone! Here's what's actually happening:

What's going on right now: DNS propagation is basically the internet's phone book updating everywhere in the world. When you change nameservers, that change has to spread across thousands of servers globally. It's not instant — it rolls out in waves.

What to expect:

  • 10 min – 2 hours — most people see it working in this window
  • Up to 48 hours — the technical maximum, though rare
  • It may even work on your phone before your computer (or vice versa) because different networks update at different speeds

How to check if it's working yet without just staring at the browser:

Go to dnschecker.org and type in havenai247.com — it shows you a world map of whether the DNS has updated in different locations. When you start seeing green checkmarks, you're getting close.

In the meantime — make sure this is done:

  • ✅ Old site deleted from Netlify
  • ✅ New site has havenai247.com added under Domain Management
  • ✅ Your ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is saved in Site Configuration → Environment Variables
  • ✅ A deploy has been triggered after adding the key

That last one is easy to miss — every time you add an environment variable you need to redeploy for it to take effect.

You're close. The hardest part is already done. 🌿

Claude responded: Absolutely!

Absolutely! Supabase is what gives Haven real user accounts, saved journals, and persistent data. Here's everything you need:

What Supabase does for Haven:

  • Real login/signup (email + password)
  • Saves journal entries per user
  • Stores chat history
  • Builds the data for therapist summary reports over time
  • Free tier handles up to 50,000 users

STEP 1 — Create your Supabase account

  1. Go to supabase.com
  2. Click "Start your project" → sign up with GitHub or email
  3. Click "New Project"
  4. Name it havenai247
  5. Create a strong database password — save it somewhere safe
  6. Choose region: US East (closest to most North American users)
  7. Click "Create new project" — takes about 2 minutes to spin up

STEP 2 — Get your API keys

Once your project is ready:

  1. Left menu → "Project Settings" (gear icon)
  2. Click "API"
  3. You'll see two things you need — copy both:
Project URL:     https://xxxxxxxxxxxx.supabase.co
Anon public key: eyJhbGci...  (long string)

STEP 3 — Create your database tables

In Supabase, left menu → "SQL Editor" → click "New query" → paste this entire block and click Run:

sql
-- Users profile table
create table profiles (
  id uuid references auth.users on delete cascade,
  first_name text,
  plan text default 'basic',
  created_at timestamp default now(),
  primary key (id)
);

-- Journal entries
create table journal_entries (
  id uuid default gen_random_uuid() primary key,
  user_id uuid references auth.users on delete cascade,
  prompt text,
  content text,
  created_at timestamp default now()
);

-- Chat history
create table chat_sessions (
  id uuid default gen_random_uuid() primary key,
  user_id uuid references auth.users on delete cascade,
  mode text default 'chat',
  messages jsonb,
  created_at timestamp default now()
);

-- Enable Row Level Security (keeps data private per user)
alter table profiles enable row level security;
alter table journal_entries enable row level security;
alter table chat_sessions enable row level security;

-- Policies (users can only see their own data)
create policy "Users see own profile" on profiles
  for all using (auth.uid() = id);

create policy "Users see own journals" on journal_entries
  for all using (auth.uid() = user_id);

create policy "Users see own chats" on chat_sessions
  for all using (auth.uid() = user_id);

Click Run — you should see "Success" for each table.

STEP 4 — Add Supabase keys to Netlify

Back in Netlify → Site Configuration → Environment Variables → add these two alongside your Anthropic key:

SUPABASE_URL        →  your Project URL
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY   →  your anon public key

STEP 5 — Tell me when that's done

Once you have those keys saved in Netlify I'll build you the updated index.html and haven-chat.js with full Supabase integration — real login, signup, saved journals, and persistent sessions all wired in and ready to go. 🌿

Actually Sean, let me just fix this a different way entirely. I'm going to give you a completely new version of the function that has better error handling and logging built in so we can see exactly what's happening.

Go to GitHub → netlify/functions/haven-chat.js → pencil icon → select all → delete → paste this:

javascript
exports.handler = async function(event) {
  const headers = {
    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
    "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "Content-Type",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  };

  if (event.httpMethod === "OPTIONS") {
    return { statusCode: 200, headers, body: "" };
  }

  const key = process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY;
  
  if (!key) {
    return {
      statusCode: 200,
      headers,
      body: JSON.stringify({ reply: "API key missing" })
    };
  }

  try {
    const { messages, system } = JSON.parse(event.body);
    const response = await fetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "x-api-key": key,
        "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        model: "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001",
        max_tokens: 1000,
        system: system || "You are Haven, a warm supportive presence.",
        messages: messages.slice(-20),
      }),
    });

    const data = await response.json();
    
    if (data.error) {
      return {
        statusCode: 200,
        headers,
        body: JSON.stringify({ reply: "API error: " + data.error.message })
      };
    }

    const reply = data.content?.[0]?.text || "I'm here with you.";
    return { statusCode: 200, headers, body: JSON.stringify({ reply }) };

  } catch (err) {
    return {
      statusCode: 200,
      headers,
      body: JSON.stringify({ reply: "Error: " + err.message })
    };
  }
};

This version will show us the exact error message in the chat instead of the generic fallback. That way when it responds we'll know precisely what's wrong.

Commit it → wait for deploy → test the chat → tell me what Haven says! 🌿
